![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/0c7d4c9f4782665ddfa9e36fa52957f308e49d6e42e75f94bb01fc998bbce219.svg)
*Hint: The matrix has the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 2\textrm{i}$ with the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/ae46b58d986d4c703470adb45128c046e6e0e572ce92593a0661e990bcb1b661.svg)*
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/eaa7fa7c58b91792b295e853a01912a5ec45edda30f5de68f5e3952a73fae014.svg)

We are given the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 2\textrm{i}$ and the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/a290109e5eb086926e15a1cffa9e11dd54b8843b3891068af7c322d10baa20de.svg)

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue $\lambda_2 = \overline{\lambda}_1$ is 
$\mathbf{v}_2 = \overline{\mathbf{v}}_1.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 2\textrm{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/1ec89bb86150c8b5002835d1f7a8f796f514e8c05f70303c833d13e922d5d390.svg)

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}](\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))+\text{i}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf w_1$ and $\mathbf w_2$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial condition ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118626/assets/b263aa33a22f008a8cc114136e985b5655cd0f097584c48311bb28eca256c2d2.svg) Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & =1[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
